# onpager_user_webhook_contact (Resource)

Manage one user's notification webhook contact with the tenant permission `user_webhook_contacts.manage`. A new request UUID creates a distinct method. An exact template slot can complete a draft in place. Control verifies the recipient on completion without sending a request to the webhook. Destroy deletes the method and clears its references in retained policy steps. Import uses `user_uuid/method_uuid`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "team_id" {
  type        = string
  description = "UUID of the team that owns the notification webhook."
}

variable "user_id" {
  type        = string
  description = "UUID of a user with access to that team's webhook."
}

variable "recipient_login" {
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
  description = "Recipient identifier understood by the notification endpoint."
}

variable "endpoint" {
  type        = string
  description = "HTTP endpoint for the notification receiver."
}

resource "onpager_team_outgoing_webhook" "personal" {
  team_id      = var.team_id
  purpose      = "notification"
  display_name = "Personal notification"
  enabled      = true

  request = {
    method        = "POST"
    endpoint      = var.endpoint
    body_format   = "json"
    body_template = "{\"login\":{{ json .Recipient.login }},\"notification\":{{ json .Notification }}}"
  }

  recipient_fields = [{
    key      = "login"
    label    = "Recipient login"
    kind     = "string"
    required = true
  }]
}

resource "terraform_data" "webhook_creation" {
  triggers_replace = [var.user_id, onpager_team_outgoing_webhook.personal.id]
}

resource "onpager_user_webhook_contact" "oncall" {
  user_id      = var.user_id
  webhook_id   = onpager_team_outgoing_webhook.personal.id
  display_name = "On-call webhook"
  values       = { login = var.recipient_login }
  request_id   = terraform_data.webhook_creation.id
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `display_name` (String) Mutable contact label of 1–200 UTF-8 characters without NUL or surrounding whitespace.
- `user_id` (String) Owner user UUID. Changing it replaces the method. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID.
- `webhook_id` (String) Accessible notification webhook definition UUID. Changing it replaces the method. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID.

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the method is enabled. A new method starts enabled. An explicit false applies a guarded update after creation. Omit or set null to preserve the current setting on import, replay and subsequent updates.
- `request_id` (String) Create request UUID. Supply a stable UUID before creation, for example from terraform_data. Keep it for retries of the same create and supply a fresh UUID when recreating a deleted contact. Changing the configured value replaces the contact. May be omitted on import. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID when set.
- `template_contact_id` (String) Contact UUID in the tenant user notification defaults template. Set it to complete the matching user's untouched draft in place and preserve its policy references. Omit to create a separate method. Changing the configured slot replaces the resource. The API does not return this value on import. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID when set.
- `values` (Map of String, Sensitive) Complete recipient field map for the webhook definition. Supply it on creation, including `{}` for a definition without required fields. On update, omission or null preserves the saved fields. An explicit map replaces them all and completes a draft, including an empty map when allowed by the definition. Keys and field types must match the definition. Up to 20 fields, 1,024 UTF-8 bytes per value and 16 KiB combined. Privileged reads and imports return saved values, which persist in Terraform state. Drafts have null values.

### Read-Only

- `draft` (Boolean) Whether this method is an uncompleted webhook draft.
- `etag` (String) The method's strong numeric ETag, sent as If-Match for PATCH and DELETE. A stale tag produces a conflict.
- `generation` (Number) Observed method verification generation, including zero. The provider sends the saved generation when completing a draft with recipient values.
- `id` (String) Stable nonzero canonical lowercase OnPager UUID.
- `verified` (Boolean) Current verification status. Completing a webhook contact confirms it immediately.

## Notification webhooks and escalation chains

Use the definition UUID of an enabled webhook with `purpose = "notification"`.
A tenant definition is available globally. For a team definition, the user
must have access to that team. The webhook defines the recipient field keys and
types. Supply their values for this user, or `values = {}` when the schema
accepts an empty object. Control verifies the completed contact without sending
an HTTP request.

A direct escalation step uses a webhook with `purpose = "escalation"`. Set
`webhook_id` in the chain step to the definition UUID. For example, a team
can use a tenant escalation webhook as follows.

```hcl
resource "onpager_escalation_chain" "alerts" {
  team_id = var.team_id
  name    = "Alert webhook"
  steps = [{
    kind       = "notify_webhook"
    webhook_id = onpager_outgoing_webhook.escalation.id
  }]
}
```

See the [tenant webhook](outgoing_webhook.md), [team webhook](team_outgoing_webhook.md)
and [escalation chain](escalation_chain.md) resources.

## Recipient updates and state

Each configured `values` map replaces the entire set of recipient values.
Omitting it on an existing contact preserves the saved fields. Reads return
the current recipient values, including on import. Terraform marks them
sensitive. Protect state and saved plans accordingly.

Updates and deletes use the method's own ETag. A stale ETag reports a conflict.
Refresh and plan again before applying the change. Completing an imported
draft also checks its observed generation. A disabled contact keeps its UUID
and can be re-enabled.

## Create identity and template contacts

Supply a stable `request_id` before the first apply. The example uses the UUID
of a built-in `terraform_data` resource. A retry with the same initial inputs
and UUID recovers the original method after a lost response. Keep the UUID
through in-place updates. Control reserves it after deletion. To recreate with
unchanged configuration, replace the corresponding `terraform_data` resource
to obtain a fresh UUID. Different request UUIDs can create multiple contacts
for the same user and channel.

To complete a draft that a user's notification policies already reference, set
`template_contact_id` to the contact slot UUID in the tenant notification
defaults. Create the user after the defaults have been applied and order the
contact after any required access grant. Control fills the matching untouched
draft in place and preserves its method UUID. A changed or occupied slot can
return a conflict. Omitting the slot creates a separate method.

Destroy deletes the owned method, including a completed draft. Policy steps
retain their positions and their method references become null. Recreating the
contact gives it a new UUID. Update the affected policies to use that UUID.

## Import

Use `user_uuid/method_uuid`. The second UUID is the personal method's `id`.
Omit `request_id` and `template_contact_id` when adopting an existing contact.
Control does not return these creation inputs. Adding them to the configuration
after import requests replacement. The read returns the current recipient fields and ETag. Omit `values` to preserve the saved fields.

Example import block

```terraform
import {
  to = onpager_user_webhook_contact.oncall
  id = "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111/55555555-5555-4555-8555-555555555555"
}
```

Equivalent CLI command

```shell
terraform import onpager_user_webhook_contact.oncall 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111/55555555-5555-4555-8555-555555555555
```


## Permissions

Requires OnPager Control 0.0.10 or later and the tenant grant
`user_webhook_contacts.manage` for the PAT or service account. An authorized administrator
can read or delete an existing method after the user loses access to its
channel. Access and transport errors retain the resource in Terraform state.
